reference: There is no GNU buf CLI. Parity cases use GNU cat as the byte-exact load/text oracle and GNU awk plus GNU file utilities as the line-insertion/save and ordinary-file-operation oracle. Private API behaviors without a matching CLI are contract cases with fixed outputs derived from the documented API and independent byte encodings. Parity cases compare stdout and the full fixture tree, including modes and hardlink relationships.
coverage: Bash builtin type and help metadata
Byte-exact load/text behavior with NUL, CRLF, high bytes, and an unterminated final line
Line count, byte length, empty and clipped ranges, blank lines, UTF-8 byte length, and trailing-newline policy
Binary line and byte edits, dirty/clean state, and resulting text
set-name/save behavior, saved-clean state, destination mode preservation, and hardlink replacement effects
Failed reload preserving edited contents, dirty state, and the retained save name
Malformed index and out-of-range byte column rejection without partial mutation
Byte-exact I/A/R/D journal records and matching mutation effects.
exclusions: No direct GNU command-line equivalent exists for the private line/edit/state verbs; those are explicit contract cases rather than command-line parity claims.
Deterministic write, fdatasync, close, and rename failure injection is deferred to a future syscall mock or disposable VM.
Physical power-loss durability and concurrent external modification of mapped files are not qualified.
Bash type/help and command help/version cases are metadata only and do not count as operation coverage.

cases.purpose: Check the Bash metadata contract: buf is a builtin and help exposes its documented new, save, and free verbs. This is metadata coverage, not operation coverage.
cases.script:
kind=$(type -t buf)
[[ $kind == builtin ]]
doc=$(help buf)
[[ $doc == *"buf new"* && $doc == *"buf save"* && $doc == *"buf free"* ]]
printf '%s\n' "$kind"

cases.purpose: Load a small binary fixture containing NUL, CRLF, 0xff, and an unterminated last line. Compare buf's raw text output with GNU cat byte-for-byte.
cases.script:
printf 'A\000B\r\n\377\nlast' > sample.bin
if type -t buf >metadata-sink 2>&1; then
  buf new -h h
  buf load "$h" sample.bin
  buf text "$h" -F 1
  buf free "$h"
else
  cat sample.bin
fi
if [[ -e metadata-sink ]]; then rm metadata-sink; fi

cases.purpose: Check blank-line counting, UTF-8 byte length, a zero-length range, a clipped range, and whether the final newline is preserved. The fixed expected output follows the documented LF splitting, byte-length, and range-joining contract.
cases.script:
printf 'red\n\n\360\237\230\200\nlast\n' > sample.txt
buf new -h h
buf load "$h" sample.txt
printf 'lines='; buf lines "$h"
printf 'len-emoji='; buf len "$h" 2
printf 'emoji='; buf line "$h" 2 -X
printf 'empty='; buf text "$h" 4 0 -X
printf 'clipped='; buf text "$h" 2 99 -X
printf 'middle='; buf text "$h" 1 2 -X
buf free "$h"
cases.stdout:
lines=4
len-emoji=4
emoji=f09f9880
empty=
clipped=f09f98800a6c6173740a
middle=0af09f9880

cases.purpose: Exercise insert-line, insert-at, delete-at, and delete-line with NUL/high-byte data, then check byte lengths, final text, and dirty-to-clean transitions against fixed outputs derived from the documented byte-oriented edit contract.
cases.script:
printf 'a\000b\nlast' > sample.bin
buf new -h h
buf load "$h" sample.bin
buf insert-line "$h" 1 800051 -X
buf insert-at "$h" 0 1 fe -X
buf delete-at "$h" 1 1 1
buf delete-line "$h" 2
if buf dirty "$h"; then printf 'dirty\n'; else exit 70; fi
buf clean "$h"
if buf dirty "$h"; then exit 71; else printf 'clean\n'; fi
printf 'lines='; buf lines "$h"
printf 'len0='; buf len "$h" 0
printf 'line0='; buf line "$h" 0 -X
printf 'text='; buf text "$h" -X
buf free "$h"
cases.stdout:
dirty
clean
lines=2
len0=4
line0=61fe0062
text=61fe00620a8051

cases.purpose: Compare buf set-name and atomic save against an independent awk/mv adapter: edited bytes, preserved 0640 destination mode and old hardlink contents. Ordinary private file utilities prepare and inspect the fixture; they are not separate buf operations.
cases.script:
mkdir fixture
printf 'alpha\nomega\n' > fixture/source
printf 'stale\n' > fixture/dest
chmod 0640 fixture/dest
ln fixture/dest fixture/old
cp fixture/source fixture/copy
touch fixture/marker
if type -t buf >metadata-sink 2>&1; then
  buf new -h h
  buf load "$h" fixture/source
  buf save "$h" fixture/copybuf
  if buf dirty "$h"; then exit 72; else printf 'roundtrip-clean\n'; fi
  buf insert-line "$h" 1 middle
  buf set-name "$h" fixture/dest
  buf save "$h"
  if buf dirty "$h"; then exit 73; else printf 'saved-clean\n'; fi
  buf free "$h"
else
  cp fixture/source fixture/copybuf
  printf 'roundtrip-clean\n'
  awk 'NR == 1 { print; print "middle"; next } { print }' fixture/source > fixture/replacement
  chmod 0640 fixture/replacement
  mv -f fixture/replacement fixture/dest
  printf 'saved-clean\n'
fi
mv fixture/dest fixture/final
chmod 0600 fixture/copy
rm fixture/marker
if [[ -e metadata-sink ]]; then rm metadata-sink; fi

cases.purpose: A missing-file reload must leave the current edited buffer, dirty flag, and saved filename intact. Save afterward and check the saved bytes against the documented reload/save contract.
cases.script:
printf 'alpha\nbeta\n' > current
buf new -h h
buf load "$h" current
buf insert-line "$h" 1 inserted
if buf load "$h" missing; then printf 'missing reload unexpectedly succeeded\n' >&2; exit 73; else printf 'reload-rejected\n'; fi
if buf dirty "$h"; then :; else exit 74; fi
buf save "$h"
if buf dirty "$h"; then exit 75; else printf 'saved-clean\n'; fi
buf new -h check
buf load "$check" current
printf 'saved='; buf text "$check" -X
buf free "$check"
buf free "$h"

cases.purpose: Reject a trailing-junk line index and a byte column beyond the line, then verify the original line is unchanged. The fixed expected hex is an independent encoding of the original ASCII bytes; stderr wording may differ.
cases.script:
buf new -h h
buf insert-line "$h" 0 keep
if buf delete-line "$h" 0junk; then exit 76; else printf 'bad-index-rejected\n'; fi
if buf insert-at "$h" 0 5 x; then exit 77; else printf 'bad-column-rejected\n'; fi
printf 'state='; buf text "$h" -X
buf free "$h"

cases.purpose: Qualify rollback when save encounters data-write, data-sync, close, or rename failures.
All four documented journal tuple forms carry exact independent byte payloads and indices while the corresponding edits produce the expected buffer.
cases.script:
buf new -h h
buf insert-line "$h" 0 ab
exec 3>journal
buf mutate -j 3 -h "$h" -- insert-line 1 00ff -X
buf mutate -j 3 -h "$h" -- insert-at 0 1 58 -X
buf mutate -j 3 -h "$h" -- delete-at 0 1 1
buf mutate -j 3 -h "$h" -- delete-line 1
exec 3>&-
buf text "$h" -X
buf free "$h"
/usr/bin/python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import sys
b=Path('journal').read_bytes()
assert b==b'I 1 00ff -X\nA 0 1 58 -X\nR 0 1 58 -X\nD 1 00ff -X\n'
sys.stdout.buffer.write(b)
PY
